title: Accelerations after collision
description: Essential: Student must state both accelerations correctly: small block = 6 m/s² (right), long board = 2 m/s² (left).

title: First relative distance
description: Essential: Student must compute the maximum relative displacement after first collision as 9/4 m (or 2.25 m).

title: Nth relative distance pattern
description: Important: Student must derive or state the pattern for the Nth interval: d_maxN = 9/4^N m.

title: Minimum board length
description: Essential: Student must sum the geometric series to find L_min = 3(1 - 1/4^N) m, and give the infinite-N limit as 3 m.

title: Velocity reversal analysis
description: Important: Student must correctly apply that the block rebounds with same speed and analyze velocity changes for each collision interval.

title: Kinematic equations setup
description: Important: Student must set up correct kinematic equations for both objects during each sliding phase until relative velocity becomes zero.

title: Friction direction confusion
description: Pitfall: Student may assign wrong friction direction on the board after the block rebounds (should oppose relative motion).

title: Sign errors in velocities
description: Pitfall: Student may mishandle signs when the block's velocity reverses after collision, leading to incorrect simultaneous equations.

title: Series sum misapplication
description: Pitfall: Student may incorrectly sum the geometric series for total length or misuse the given formula.
